# Poker etiquette at a home game

*String bets, acting out of turn, slow-rolling and the other habits that make a game fun — or ruin it.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

Etiquette isn’t about being formal. It keeps the game fair, fast and friendly, so people want to come back next week. These are the habits that matter most.

## Act in turn

Wait until the player on your right has acted. Folding, betting or even reaching for your chips early gives away information and changes how others play. If you plan to fold, just wait — it takes two seconds.

## Make your bets clear

- **Say it out loud** (“raise to 30”) or push the full amount forward in **one motion**.
- No **string bets**: putting some chips in, then going back for more, only counts as a call unless you announced a raise first.
- Facing a bet, a single big chip without a word is a **call**. Say “raise” if you mean it.
- Don’t **splash the pot** — stack your bet in front of you so everyone can see and count it.

## Showdown manners

- **Never slow-roll.** If you know you have the winning hand, show it straight away. Making someone think they’ve won and then turning over the nuts is the rudest move in poker.
- **Table your hand** — turn both cards face up and let the cards speak.
- **Don’t muck early.** Keep your cards until the pot is pushed.

## Keep hands clean

- **One player to a hand.** Don’t advise someone during a hand, even a beginner.
- **Don’t talk about folded cards** while a hand is still being played. “I folded a seven” can change the outcome.
- **Protect your cards** with a chip or your hand, so they aren’t mixed into the muck by accident.
- **Keep your chips visible** and stacked neatly — bigger chips in front, easy to count.

## Being a good guest

- Be gentle with beginners. Explain the rules between hands, not in the middle of one.
- No gloating, no blaming the dealer for the cards.
- Keep an eye on the pace: phone down when it’s your turn.
- If you plan to leave early, say so when you sit down. Leaving right after a big win (“hit and run”) is allowed but feels better when announced.
- Help tidy up and count chips at the end.

> **Tip — When in doubt, ask:** Not sure if an action is allowed? Ask before you do it. Nobody minds a question; everybody minds an argument.
